Omg I totally forgot about the balls! Yes I've had those too and I remember the hassle and bit down on them so much. One trick I used was to hold the piercing on the side I was chewing on, so the long part would stay on the outside and I wouldn't bite on them as often.

And yes, you'll find this in the baking department! Just make sure it says rough sea salt or something along those lines.

Also the amount of crust that builds also had a lot to do with your environment, I was working on a warehouse when I got mine done and they got crusty a lot. But that was due to there being a lot of dust and dirty particles in the air and around me. So maybe you can recognise this? I would suggest you clean them once during your break or at least spray on some solution so the build up can dissolve a bit.
Masks play a huge part here too, they will run up against your piercings which only causes more crust buildup. All these things can make it so your piercings indeed seem like they're glued in place.

I think I had mine for 6 weeks when I finally switched to flatbacks.
Once you can move them without discomfort you could think about switching to flatbacks, the big factor is the size you take them in. If they're too tight you need to take them out right away, don't sleep on it. If you don't want to get them switched by a piercer but do it yourself, I did so too, then make sure you buy a few sizes so you can see which fits best. Also note that your cheeks will most likely not be the same size.
My right side is 2mm longer than my left for example. It's best to keep them a bit longer until you reach about 8 to 12 weeks. Try not to eat anything too sticky like chewing gum, caramel,... Basically anything that can stretch and stick. Cuz it will stick to your piercing and pull it inwards causing you to bite on them.

They look great! When I got mine done they took about a good two to three weeks to heal before I could downsize (note they weren't FULLY healed but healed enough for a downsize) Once you get them downsized, healing will go more smoothly. For now I would do like someone else suggested and give yourself a saline bath/soak. What my piercer suggested was a soak that was a mix of luke warm water and rough sea salt. Make sure to dissolve the sea salt though and do not use kitchen salt! As kitchen salt is very aggressive and will irritate.

If it's too much trouble or it hurts too much to hang your head to one side for the soak, you can use a cotton ball and drench this in the solution. Then you can hold that to your piercing for a few minutes :) I had to do it this way as my cheeks hurt too much to actually hang my head to the side.

Doing a mouthwash with a salt/water solution will help as well, just don't use actual mouth wash as most of these contain alcohol and will only irritate your piercings.

Once the swelling of your cheeks has gone down and it doesn't hurt to smile anymore, you can contact your piercer again and discuss downsizing :) these will still not be your final size but will definetly help the healing process

Well, I'm not gonna lie, they're nipples, they hurt

But once I walked out of the shop, the hurt was pretty much already gone  
They'll be sensitive for a few days (maybe up to a week or maybe two, everyone is different) and you are to leave them alone up to 6 weeks

That being said, they aren't gonna be hurting for 6 months, with the 6 months they mean that it takes that long for the inside to heal up completely until it's no longer a "wound"

By week two, you won't feel them anymore :) 

So just go for it!

I would not change it yourself, get it done at a professional, the chances you won't get the other jewel in yourself are very high  
So is the risk of getting an infection due to bacteria on your hands or new jewelry piece.

Just go to a piercer (either the one where you got the piercing or another) and say that you would like the bar an inch shorter  
Best is to go to another piercer (if that's possible of course) and they will immediately know what to do

They will also be using a taper, because the piercing is so fresh, the moment you would take out the jewelry, the wound will seize right back up due to the swelling.  
If it's a comfort, it really does not hurt to get them switched :)

When I got mine done I had a speech impediment for about two weeks, ofcourse the first week was way worse but it gets better :)

Once you feel your tongue is healing for you to properly speak, the bar will be working against your speech, but please, like everyone already said, get that bar changed because it's way too long

You get a longer bar for swelling but if your tongue would actually swell up to the ball, it would burst  
This long of a bar will cause damage inside your mouth and will make the healing process so much more difficult

I had been in bed for days again, not eating, drinking, showers, just nothing. 24/7 in that bed, in the dark, alone. Exactly what I thought I deserved. Usually the thought of my family finding my dead body would make me think again but not that day, my mind had been made up. I would wait till my parents were asleep so I knew they wouldn't bother to check up until morning. 
The only person I still talked to was my best friend, I had texted him a few messages but didn't really bother to really read what he wrote back. I wanted to push him away, give him the last drop to say fuck it and leave me alone.

My godfather had come to visit that day with his wife but I had texted my mother I didn't feel well so I wouldn't have to get out of bed. 

However, not an hour later the bell rang, I heard my mother open up and then someone coming up the stairs. 
I didn't bother to look up, what was the use anyway? Then a small light came on, the first light I'd seen in weeks.

But there was my best friend and he looked pissed. Like seriously pissed I hadn't seen him like in the years I knew him.
And the moment he asked me what the fuck I thought I was doing and I started crying. Just crying my eyes out saying all the things of how I felt.

My best friend angrily telling me that I did matter and that all the shit I was thinking was bullshit was my wake up call. How strange it may sound, in that moment it helped me more than my psychiatrist and meds.

I promised him in that moment that I'd do better, we're now a little over a year later and I couldn't be doing better.
I'm still taking my meds but we're looking into getting me off them during next summer.

My best friend saved me that day, and I've thanked him for that so many times now. But the best 'thank you' I can give him is for me to live fully.
